title: SDLC event
description: A structured event emitted by the SDLC. The notification subsystem consumes these; it never polls, and it is never the event source. Events are facts about the past, named in the past tense. correlation_id ties every event about one change together and causation_id names the event that caused this one, so one change's whole timeline can be reconstructed forwards and walked backwards from any point in it.

id.description: EVT-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS-nnnn. Stable, so a duplicate delivery is detectable.

level.description: Mirrors the SDLC hierarchy. Worker-level events are recorded and, by default, not notified.

subject.description: The artifact or work item this is about. Also the default thread key.

actor.description: What caused it: an agent role, a human role, or - when the emitter supplies nothing finer - the emitting stage or cycle id from the catalogue. Never a person's name.

correlates.description: Related artifact ids, so a feature's whole timeline can be reconstructed.

payload.description: Facts only. No prose, no formatting, no recipient list. Routing is the policy engine's job and wording is the agent's.

category.description: Coarse grouping for audit queries and for digest sections.

actor_type.description: What kind of actor caused it. A human actor is a role, never a person's name.

severity.description: The event's own severity, independent of the routing priority the policy assigns.

status.description: Where the thing this event is about now stands.

correlation_id.description: Ties every event about one change together across workflows: the feature id usually, the incident id during an incident. Required. Defaults to the subject, which is correct only for the event that opens a thread - pass it explicitly for everything downstream.

artifact.description: The artifact id this event concerns. Defaults to the subject, so an audit query can filter on one field without knowing which event types put the id in which place.

stage.description: Macro stage id, denormalised from source for querying. Derived from the catalogue's emitted_by when the emitter does not pass one.

cycle.description: Department cycle id, denormalised from source for querying. Derived from the catalogue's emitted_by when the emitter does not pass one.

workflow.description: Workflow id, denormalised from source for querying. Derived from the catalogue's emitted_by when the emitter does not pass one. Absent for guard- and schedule-sourced events, which belong to no workflow.

causation_id.description: The id of the event that caused this one. Absent only on the event that opens a correlation thread. Present everywhere else, which is what makes the chain walkable backwards from any point; correlation_id alone gives a set, not an order.

schema_version.description: Event model version. '1' is an event written before correlation and causation were enforced: it may lack causation_id, actor, artifact and severity. '2' carries all of them. Readers must not assume a v1 event is broken.
